issues.legal_issue: A jagirdar is entitled to compensation for unbuilt village-site land in which the jagirdar had a right or interest extinguished by abolition.
material_facts: The abolition vested unbuilt village-site lands in the State and extinguished rights held by jagirdars in that property.
The jagirdars claimed compensation for unbuilt village-site lands in which they had rights or interests.
issues.conclusion: The jagirdars were entitled to compensation for all unbuilt village-site lands in which they could prove a right or interest.
issues.legal_principle: Section 8 of the Bombay Merged Territories and Areas (Jagirs Abolition) Act, 1953 vested the specified properties, including unbuilt village-site lands, in the State and extinguished jagirdars’ rights. Section 11(3) is to be construed as entitling a jagirdar to compensation for rights or interests in such property under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, subject to the exceptions in section 11(3)(i) to (iii).

predicates.jagir_abolition_compensation_case: The proceeding concerns compensation for rights or interests extinguished when jagir property vested in the State.
predicates.unbuilt_village_site_land_vested_in_stat: The land at issue is unbuilt village-site land that vested in the State on abolition.
predicates.jagirdar_proved_extinguished_interest: The jagirdar proved a right or interest in the land that was extinguished.

issues.definition: When an abolition-compensation case concerns unbuilt village-site land vested in the State and the jagirdar proves an extinguished interest in it, compensation is awarded for that land.

issues.legal_issue: Solatium is not payable on compensation awarded for abolition of jagirs under the Act.
material_facts: The jagirdars sought solatium in addition to compensation for property rights extinguished by jagir abolition.
The Act’s explanation defining market value referred to section 23(1), but not section 23(2), of the Land Acquisition Act.
The Act required awards to be in the form prescribed by section 26(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, whose prescribed form did not mention solatium.
issues.conclusion: The jagirdars were not entitled to solatium on the compensation awarded under the Act.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished State of Gujarat v. Vakhtsinghji Sursinghji Vaghela, which concerned the Taluqdari Act and its express provisions. Under sections 11, 13 and 15 of the Jagirs Abolition Act, the reference to section 23(1), rather than section 23(2), of the Land Acquisition Act, and the required award form under section 26(1), showed that solatium was not provided. Solatium under section 23(2) is additional compensation for the compulsory nature of acquisition. R. D. Suryanarayana Rao v. Revenue Divisional Officer and Kesireddi Appala Swamy v. Special Tehsildar were approved on the distinction between compensation in the award and solatium; Maharaj Umeg Singh v. State of Bombay was cited regarding the Act as agrarian reform.

predicates.jagir_abolition_compensation_case: The proceeding concerns compensation for property rights extinguished by abolition of jagirs.
predicates.statute_uses_market_value_without_compul: The governing compensation scheme refers to market-value compensation but does not provide the additional amount associated with compulsory acquisition.
predicates.statute_prescribes_award_form_without_th: The governing scheme requires an award in a prescribed form that does not include the additional compulsory-acquisition amount.

issues.definition: When the abolition-compensation scheme provides market-value compensation without the compulsory-acquisition addition and its required award form omits that addition, solatium is not awarded.

issues.legal_issue: Interest on compensation instalments paid late is payable on the delayed principal amounts but not on instalments of interest, with the period of delay calculated separately for each principal instalment.
material_facts: The jagirdars were deprived of their property when the Act came into force, but their bonds were delivered about ten years later.
The bonds carried interest and were repayable in annual instalments; because of the delay, multiple instalments became payable together upon delivery of the bonds.
The High Court awarded interest on the delayed instalments, including their interest components, and treated all principal instalments as delayed for the same period.
issues.conclusion: Interest was payable on the principal amount of each delayed instalment, but not on the interest component; the first instalment accrued interest for nine years, the second for eight years, and so on, with the last accruing interest for one year.
issues.legal_principle: Section 22 of the Jagirs Abolition Act provided for interest-bearing bonds and annual instalments; rules 4 and 5 treated the bonds as issued from the Act’s commencement and made overdue instalments payable on delivery. Applying the principle in Satinder Singh v. Amrao Singh, interest is justified where taking possession deprives the owner of the property and its income pending payment. Interest is payable on delayed principal, not on interest already due, and the delay is measured separately for each instalment.

predicates.jagir_abolition_compensation_case: The proceeding concerns compensation payable under a jagir-abolition scheme.
predicates.property_taken_before_compensation_paid: The claimant was deprived of the property before receiving the compensation due for it.
predicates.bond_delivery_delayed_multiple_instalmen: Delivery of the compensation bonds was delayed until multiple instalments had fallen due and were paid together.

issues.definition: When a jagir-abolition claimant loses the property before payment and delayed bond delivery causes multiple instalments to be paid together, interest is awarded only on each principal instalment for its own period of delay.

issues.legal_issue: The expression “three multiples” means three times the assessment, not six times the assessment.
material_facts: The jagirdars argued that the expression “three multiples” in the compensation provision meant six times the land assessment.
The Act used both “three times” and “three multiples” in different provisions.
issues.conclusion: “Three multiples” meant three times the assessment, and there was no material difference between the two expressions.
issues.legal_principle: The Court read the expressions in context and found that their use in different provisions reflected no intended variation. “Three multiples” was used in its ordinary, common-parlance sense, not as a technical mathematical expression.

predicates.jagir_abolition_compensation_case: The proceeding concerns compensation under a jagir-abolition scheme.
predicates.compensation_formula_uses_three_multiple: The compensation formula describes the amount as three multiples of the land assessment.

issues.definition: When a jagir-abolition compensation formula uses “three multiples” of assessment, the multiplier means three times the assessment.

issues.legal_issue: A separate levy collected in respect of irrigated land is not part of the land assessment for calculating compensation when it was recorded separately from the assessment.
material_facts: The jagirdars collected Bagayat kas on land with irrigation facilities in addition to the land assessment.
The records showed Bagayat kas separately from the land assessment.
The jagirdars argued that the levy should be included in the assessment used to calculate compensation.
issues.conclusion: Bagayat kas was not part of the land assessment for calculating compensation, and no separate compensation for the lost levy could be awarded in the absence of legislative provision.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 11(2) of the Jagirs Abolition Act, compensation was calculated by reference to the assessment for the land. The separate recording and imposition of Bagayat kas indicated that it was a distinct levy rather than part of that assessment. The Court stated that any separate compensation for loss of the levy was for the legislature to provide.

predicates.jagir_abolition_compensation_case: The proceeding concerns compensation under a jagir-abolition scheme.
predicates.land_assessment_used_for_compensation: The compensation calculation is based on the assessment fixed for the land.
predicates.additional_irrigation_levy_recorded_sepa: A charge associated with irrigation was imposed in addition to, and recorded separately from, the land assessment.

issues.definition: When compensation is based on land assessment and an irrigation-related charge was separately imposed and recorded, that separate charge is excluded from the assessment.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court will not interfere under its special-leave jurisdiction with the reduction of compensation rates where the overall factual result does not warrant interference.
material_facts: The State had no right of appeal to the Revenue Tribunal under the Act but persuaded the Tribunal, in the jagirdars’ appeal, to reduce some village-site land compensation rates.
The Tribunal also increased the area of village-site land eligible for compensation, and the net compensation payable to the jagirdars increased.
The Tribunal’s factual decision was not found to be erroneous.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to interfere with the Tribunal’s decision on the compensation rates.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 16 and 17 of the Jagirs Abolition Act did not give the State a right of appeal to the Tribunal. The Court considered that there might be substance in the argument that the State could not challenge the rates under Order 41 Rule 22 of the Code of Civil Procedure, referring to The Management of Itakhoolie Tea Estate v. Its Workmen. Nevertheless, taking the totality of the circumstances and the factual result, the Court declined to interfere under Article 136 of the Constitution.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal_from_compensation_decision and state_lacked_appeal_right and tribunal_reduced_rates_in_opponent_appeal and tribunal_increased_compensable_area and net_compensation_increased and factual_decision_not_erroneous

predicates.special_leave_appeal_from_compensation_d: The proceeding is a special-leave appeal challenging a compensation decision.
predicates.state_lacked_appeal_right: The State had no right of appeal to the tribunal from the original compensation decision.
predicates.tribunal_reduced_rates_in_opponent_appea: The tribunal reduced some compensation rates while deciding an appeal brought by the opposing claimant.
predicates.tribunal_increased_compensable_area: The tribunal increased the area for which compensation was payable.
predicates.net_compensation_increased: The overall amount payable after the tribunal’s decision increased despite the reduced rates.
predicates.factual_decision_not_erroneous: The tribunal’s factual decision was not found to be erroneous.

issues.definition: When a special-leave compensation appeal concerns rate reductions made in the opponent’s appeal, but the State lacked an appeal right, the compensable area and net award increased, and the factual decision was not erroneous, special-leave interference is declined.
